title: Dual roles of host N-glycosylation in enteropathogenic Escherichia coli infection.
authors: Cohen Yaron, Klil; Socol, Yaakov; Yedidi, Noam; Bejerano-Sagie, Michal; Ravins, Miriam; Fine-Leebhoff, Shira; Birimberg-Schwartz, Liron; Grunewald, Myriam; Hullahalli, Karthik; de Sousa Vieira, Afonso; Waldor, Matthew K; Bartfeld, Sina; Ben-Yehuda, Sigal; Rosenshine, Ilan
one_liner_zh: 该研究利用CRISPR-Cas9筛选鉴定宿主N-糖基化在EPEC感染中的作用，虽使用CRISPR筛选但对象与机制均非核酸酶切割或碱基编辑，仅作为工具应用，与本课题无实质关联。
abstract: Host factors determine pathogen tropism but knowledge of host genes facilitating enteropathogenic Escherichia coli (EPEC) infection is limited. To identify host determinants required for infection by EPEC, we performed two independent genome-scale CRISPR-Cas9 screens. Both converged on host N-glycosylation as a critical requirement for infection. Genetic or pharmacological inhibition of N-glycan maturation revealed that N-glycosylation promotes infection through two distinct pathways. First, N-linked poly-N-acetyllactosamine glycans serve as receptors for the major EPEC adhesin, the bundle-forming pilus (BFP). Second, perturbation of N-glycosylation compromises host membrane structure, resulting in reduced type III secretion system activity, independently of host cell attachment. Using epithelial monolayers derived from human colon and jejunum organoids, we further show that EPEC attachment inversely correlates with terminal mannose exposure, suggesting glycan composition may be involved in determining intestinal tropism. Together, these findings establish host N-glycan maturation as a key host pathway exploited during enteric infection.
abstract_zh: 宿主因子决定病原体嗜性，但关于促进肠致病性大肠杆菌（EPEC）感染的宿主基因知识有限。为鉴定EPEC感染所需的宿主决定因素，我们进行了两次独立的基因组规模CRISPR-Cas9筛选。两次筛选均聚焦于宿主N-糖基化作为感染的关键需求。通过遗传或药理学抑制N-聚糖成熟，发现N-糖基化通过两条不同途径促进感染。首先，N-连接的多聚N-乙酰乳糖胺聚糖作为主要EPEC黏附素——束状菌毛（BFP）的受体。其次，N-糖基化的扰动损害宿主膜结构，导致III型分泌系统活性降低，且与宿主细胞附着无关。利用源自人结肠和空肠类器官的上皮单层，我们进一步表明EPEC附着与末端甘露糖暴露呈负相关，提示聚糖组成可能参与决定肠道嗜性。综合这些发现，确立了宿主N-聚糖成熟作为肠道感染期间被利用的关键宿主途径。
